section_summary: This section follows the dispute over Japan’s Petroleum Industry Law, especially the six-month oil-storage requirement, sales quotas and compensation sought by foreign oil companies. Embassy reports and State Department correspondence trace negotiations through late 1935 and discuss possible further representations. Navy and Interior Department material addresses Japanese efforts to secure oil abroad and the volume and prices of U.S. oil exports to Japan.

subfiles.title: American oil interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, U.S. Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s oil-storage postponement, Korean sales quotas and North Sakhalin production.
subfiles.summary: The despatch considers whether postponing the six-month storage rule will help foreign companies and concludes that formal U.S. intervention is premature. It reports proposed protests over reduced quotas in Korea, declining Japanese production in North Sakhalin, and press criticism of the storage law.

subfiles.title: The Oil Storage Concession
subfiles.about: Comments on the postponement of Japan’s compulsory oil-storage requirement.
subfiles.summary: The editorial views postponement as a sign that economic objections prevailed and that military concern over an imminent crisis had eased.

subfiles.title: Letter on Japan’s Control Law
subfiles.from: P. W. Parker, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Advises that Standard-Vacuum is considering Japan’s latest action under the Control Law.
subfiles.summary: Parker says the company may later seek a discussion with the State Department.

subfiles.title: Reply to Parker on Japan’s oil regulations
subfiles.about: Summarizes the Embassy’s report on Japan’s revised oil-storage and compensation proposals.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck outlines the postponed six-month storage requirement, proposed compensation, possible price increases and the effect on foreign companies’ quotas. He invites further discussion.

subfiles.title: Digest of Tokyo despatch No. 1506
subfiles.about: Summarizes the Embassy’s report on foreign companies’ dissatisfaction with Japan’s oil policy.
subfiles.summary: The digest notes that storage duties remain, while compensation and prices remain unsettled.

subfiles.title: American oil interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, U.S. Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese officials’ explanation of oil-storage obligations and the foreign companies’ objections.
subfiles.summary: Officials maintain that six-month stocks are required but propose compensation for part of the carrying cost, later gasoline-price relief and larger quotas for companies already storing oil. Standard-Vacuum and Rising Sun argue that this departs from the April five-point understanding and requires unacceptable new investment. The despatch also discusses temporary use of their Dairen tanks and referral of the dispute to company headquarters.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Tokyo oil despatches to London
subfiles.about: Encloses Tokyo despatches Nos. 1482 and 1506.
subfiles.summary: Forwards two Embassy reports on Japan’s oil situation.

subfiles.title: Appointment request on Petroleum Control Law
subfiles.about: Requests a meeting for Parker and G. S. Walden.
subfiles.summary: Parker seeks an appointment to discuss Japan’s Petroleum Control Law.

subfiles.title: Reply arranging meeting with Parker and Walden
subfiles.about: Offers a time to discuss the Petroleum Control Law.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck proposes a Wednesday afternoon meeting.

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum’s position on the Control Law
subfiles.from: P. W. Parker, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Relays the company’s cable urging adherence to the April five-point memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Parker reports a position reached after consultation with British oil interests.

subfiles.title: Correction to Standard-Vacuum’s October 31 letter
subfiles.about: Corrects a statement about the company’s compliance with the storage law.
subfiles.summary: The company asks Hornbeck to replace its earlier letter because the six-month requirement had been postponed.

subfiles.title: Revised statistics on oil shipments to Japan
subfiles.from: P. W. Parker, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Provides Pacific Coast oil-shipment figures and explains their increase.
subfiles.summary: Parker reports higher 1935 crude, diesel and fuel-oil shipments, projecting more than 20 million barrels for the year. He attributes the rise chiefly to Japanese stockholding and naval storage, followed by consumption growth and lower California crude prices.

subfiles.title: Original statistics on oil shipments to Japan
subfiles.from: P. W. Parker, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Provides the same shipment figures with an incorrect statement about compliance.
subfiles.summary: This version says the foreign companies were not complying with the law; a later correction explains that postponement made them compliant.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about November 6 oil conference
subfiles.about: Requests the results of a conference between Japanese officials and foreign oil interests.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks whether the meeting occurred and what it achieved.

subfiles.title: Note on Tokyo’s telegram No. 211
subfiles.about: Records that no immediate departmental action is needed.
subfiles.summary: Standard-Vacuum already has the conference results and has promised to report its decision.

subfiles.title: Results of the November 6 oil conference
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s refusal to renegotiate the six-month stockholding obligation.
subfiles.summary: Yoshino and Kurusu say the April memorandum was an aspiration, not a promise, and that the six-month requirement is settled. Companies must decide whether to continue trading under the law; officials request a prompt answer for compensation-budget planning.

subfiles.title: Naval Intelligence transmittal of oil-development report
subfiles.about: Forwards a naval report on a proposed Japanese overseas oil corporation.
subfiles.summary: Puleston sends the report for State Department information and filing.

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese overseas oil-development corporation
subfiles.from: W. T. Tarrant, Eleventh Naval District
subfiles.about: Highlights a Japanese proposal to acquire foreign oil fields.
subfiles.summary: The report draws attention to a reported Mexican offer and the recent visit of former president Abelardo Rodríguez.

subfiles.title: Japanese news item on overseas oil fields
subfiles.about: Describes plans for a subsidized Japanese corporation to survey and acquire foreign oil fields.
subfiles.summary: Proposed surveys cover Mexico, other Latin American countries, Borneo and Java.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Naval Intelligence report
subfiles.about: Thanks Puleston for the translated Japanese newspaper item.
subfiles.summary: Duggan acknowledges the clipping on a Japanese overseas oil-development corporation.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to despatch No. 1515
subfiles.about: Points to another file entry concerning American oil interests in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Neville’s despatch No. 1515.

subfiles.title: American oil interests in Japan
subfiles.about: Recaps the storage postponement and September talks with Japanese officials.
subfiles.summary: The excerpt records the six-month requirement, possible compensation, reduced foreign-company quotas and the companies’ objection that these terms breach the April understanding.

subfiles.title: Digest of Tokyo despatch No. 1534
subfiles.about: Summarizes gasoline-price and possible Chinese-company developments.
subfiles.summary: The digest notes a 2½-sen gasoline-price increase and questions how a proposed Chinese-company acquisition relates to the Oil Control Law.

subfiles.title: American oil interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, U.S. Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports a gasoline-price increase and foreign companies’ response to Japanese oil policy.
subfiles.summary: Japan approved a 2½-sen-per-gallon gasoline increase. Standard-Vacuum continued to invoke the April memorandum, while foreign interests considered buying Japanese refiners’ surplus products through a Chinese concern.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Standard-Vacuum representatives
subfiles.about: Records an extended discussion of Standard-Vacuum’s options under Japan’s oil law.
subfiles.summary: Company representatives reject further capital investment for six-month stocks and consider withdrawal, reduced operations, approaches to Japanese military authorities and use of hydrogenation patents in negotiations. State Department officers discuss treaty arguments and possible retaliation, while noting doubts about their effectiveness and risks to U.S. trade. No course is settled pending further reports from Japan and British consultations.

subfiles.title: Transmission of November 6 conversation to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Encloses the memorandum of conversation with Standard-Vacuum representatives.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the November 6 discussion for the Embassy’s information.

subfiles.title: Transmission of November 6 conversation to London
subfiles.about: Encloses the memorandum of conversation with Standard-Vacuum representatives.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the November 6 discussion for the Ambassador’s information.

subfiles.title: Conversation with the British Ambassador
subfiles.about: Records Britain’s request for renewed joint representations to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The British Ambassador asks the U.S. and British embassies in Tokyo to press for the April five-point program. Hamilton agrees to seek the Tokyo Embassy’s judgment and awaits Standard-Vacuum’s decision.

subfiles.title: Draft instruction seeking Tokyo’s opinion
subfiles.about: Asks whether further representations to Japan would be useful.
subfiles.summary: The Department requests consultation with British and Standard-Vacuum representatives and advice on any proposed approach.

subfiles.title: Transmission of recent oil correspondence to London
subfiles.about: Encloses conversation memoranda and Tokyo telegram No. 224.
subfiles.summary: Forwards recent material on proposed representations over Japan’s oil law.

subfiles.title: Transmission of conversation memoranda to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Encloses November 27 and December 2 conversation memoranda.
subfiles.summary: Forwards memoranda on the British and Standard-Vacuum discussions.

subfiles.title: Instruction seeking Tokyo’s opinion
subfiles.about: Seeks advice on renewed joint representations to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The sent telegram asks the Embassy to consult its British colleague and Standard-Vacuum before recommending whether and how to act.

subfiles.title: Enclosure charge slip
subfiles.about: Records handling of an enclosure associated with the file.
subfiles.summary: A filing slip tracks an enclosure and its return.

subfiles.title: Telephone call to the British Ambassador
subfiles.about: Records Hornbeck’s communication of Tokyo’s latest view.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck relays telegram No. 224 and says the Department will contact the American oil companies.

subfiles.title: Tokyo’s recommendation on further representations
subfiles.about: Recommends a timely joint approach backed by the companies’ commercial position.
subfiles.summary: Embassy and company representatives favor further representations, but believe a simple request to restore the April program would have little effect. They suggest that company headquarters decide whether to state that six-month storage could cause withdrawal from Japan.

subfiles.title: Transmission of paraphrased Tokyo telegram to Parker
subfiles.about: Sends Parker a confidential paraphrase of Tokyo’s telegram.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck provides the paraphrase for Parker’s discreet use.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Tokyo telegram No. 224
subfiles.about: Restates Tokyo’s recommendation for stronger representations.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase says a renewed approach should indicate what the companies would do if onerous storage rules remain.

subfiles.title: Instruction on Embassy participation in oil discussions
subfiles.about: Sets limits on Embassy action while companies consider further steps.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy may join appropriate discussions but must report developments and await instructions before approaching Japanese authorities or firms.

subfiles.title: Further instruction on a possible company trade
subfiles.about: Explains the Department’s position on a possible commercial offer to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department says government agencies should not join a proposed trade involving an industrial process. It takes no official position on the offer and outlines limits on contacts with Japanese military authorities.

subfiles.title: Supplement on Standard-Vacuum instructions
subfiles.about: Reports receipt of the company’s instructions and an amendment.
subfiles.summary: The Department has received Standard-Vacuum’s instructions and a December 11 amendment.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Bureau of Mines memorandum
subfiles.from: Harold L. Ickes, Secretary of the Interior
subfiles.about: Sends a Bureau of Mines memorandum on oil exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Ickes forwards the memorandum and asks for its return.

subfiles.title: Oil exports to Japan and California prices
subfiles.from: John W. Finch, Director, Bureau of Mines
subfiles.about: Provides monthly export figures, values and California oil-price data.
subfiles.summary: Finch supplies tables for principal oil exports to Japan through October 1935 and California domestic prices. He explains why export and domestic prices differ and reports estimates of at least twelve months of Japanese oil stocks, including more than 3.5 million barrels held by the military.
